result:
I added `migrations/003_exports_status_default.sql`. I haven't run it against a database.

It does three things:
1. It sets any existing NULL `status` rows to `'queued'`. Without this, adding NOT NULL would fail on those rows.
2. It sets the column default to `'queued'`.
3. It makes the column NOT NULL.

I left `001_init.sql` alone because it may already be applied, and editing it wouldn't change an existing database.

The backfill marks every existing NULL row as `'queued'`, including any that already ran or finished. If you'd rather give those a different status, change the first statement.

I didn't check whether any code inserts into `exports` with an explicit NULL status. If something does, it will start failing once the constraint is in place.
